## Project context
We are building a Support Ticket Management System.
- Backend: Java 21, Spring Boot 3.x, Spring Web, Spring Data JPA, Bean Validation
- Database: PostgreSQL in normal runs, H2 only for tests (or file-based H2 for local dev)
- API: REST + JSON
- Frontend: React (Vite) or Next.js
- Build/test: Maven, JUnit 5, Spring Boot Test, MockMvc
- AI tools: Cursor, GitHub Copilot

search by keyword, filter by status, persist data, validate input on the backend, and show clear errors in the UI.

I added **`CONSTITUTION.md`** at the repo root. It is the single source of truth for Spec-Driven Development on TicketFlow. Summary:

### Precedence
Constitution → feature spec → plan → tasks → code. Nothing below this document may override it without an explicit amendment.

### Locked stack
Java 21, Spring Boot 3.x (Web, Data JPA, Bean Validation), PostgreSQL at runtime, H2 for tests, REST/JSON, Maven + JUnit 5/MockMvc, React (Vite) **or** Next.js (one choice fixed in the first frontend spec).

### Architecture
Thin REST layer, services for use cases, JPA-only persistence, modular monolith, server-generated IDs, `/api/v1/` camelCase JSON.

### Domain (MVP)
Tickets (title, description, priority, assignee, status), comments, keyword search, status filter—with invariants spelled out for enums, search behavior, and concurrency (last-write-wins).

### Quality bar
Bean Validation on the backend; stable error shape for the UI; tests required for services, APIs, and non-trivial queries; `mvn test` green before “done.”

### AI rules
Read constitution + active spec first, match `org.ticketflow.*` patterns, minimal diffs, no guessing on unclear requirements.

### Out of scope (until amended)
Auth, multi-tenancy, attachments, email/SLA, realtime push.
